hook_text: A river bank in Alexandra covered in bottles and bags, every one of them going to outlive you.
clip_script: Plastic does not rot. South Africa makes about 2.4 million tonnes of plastic waste a year and recycles about 14 per cent. The rest blocks drains, chokes rivers, kills animals. Three tools, in order. Reduce: use less. Cloth bag, refillable bottle, thinner packaging. Reuse: same item again. Bottle to water bottle, bucket to planter, returnable crate. Recycle: collect, sort, wash, melt, remould, but only clean PET, HDPE, polypropylene and film, and mostly collected by waste pickers paid by the kilogram. Why that order? Each step down costs more and gets back less, and every remelt loses quality. So reduce first, reuse second, recycle what is left, and keep your clean recyclables in a separate bag for the people who collect them.
visual_style: Whiteboard river with bottles, a 14 per cent slice of a bar, three stacked boxes reduce reuse recycle with cost arrows growing downward, a picker's trolley to a buy-back centre, a bottle degrading to fibre to carpet.
mood: Clear-eyed and practical, like a clean-up morning.
pacing: Problem, figures, three Rs in order, who collects, limits.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and start a separate clean-recyclables bag at home this week.
